newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher on stronger debt, budget.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher on stronger debt, budget.

text.p: The Swedish sharemarket gained in subdued trade on Friday as debt yields fell and the Swedish government presented a confident budget to parliament.
The bourse's general index closed 0.62 percent higher at 2,042.03 in turnover of 2.5 billion crowns.

"The market feels relatively strong...but it is not entirely free of worries. The crown has strengthened considerably and if it stays that way it could mean a revision of currency effects for export companies," a broker said.
The banking sector outperformed the rest of the market with the sector index rising 2.0 percent as debt yields fell.
Handelsbanken ended 5.50 crowns higher at 154.50 and S-E-Banken rose 1.50 crowns to 59.
Drug company Astra ended the day one crown lower at 275 after having touched 279 during the session.
Telecoms group Ericsson ended flat at 166 crowns.
Many investors turned towards defensive cyclical shares such forestry company SCA, which rose two crowns to 136, and gas firm AGA, which ended 3.0 crowns up at 108.
The market was now focusing on the Fed's meeting on Tuesday.
